summary: Final consistency re-review of PR #129. The learnings.jsonl and deleted-agent path references are clean in md/json/mjs/toml files (those fixes landed). However, found 4 stale deleted-agent NAME references in agent definitions and skill docs that the previous fix missed because the grep patterns only matched path-style references. The orchestrator TypeScript runtime has extensive stale references to deleted agents but was not modified by this PR (separate scope). One workflow script issue with QA context passing.

findings.issue: Handoff section references deleted agent 'design-ux' as a valid nextStage target: 'nextStage: implementer (or design-ux if the spec is novel UI...)'. Propagated to .claude/agents/architect.md:89 and .codex/agents/architect.toml:75. If architect follows this instruction in the programmatic path, loadAgentPrompt('design-ux') will ENOENT because agents/design-ux.md was deleted.
findings.fix: Remove the '(or design-ux if...)' parenthetical. The implementer now owns all code including UI. Re-run yarn sync to propagate.

findings.issue: loopBackTo clamped targets list includes 'debugger' (deleted agent) and says 'never forward to integrator or release' (release is deleted). Line reads: 'loopBackTo is clamped to product-spec / architect / implementer / debugger'. This is a kernel file shared across repos.
findings.fix: Change to: 'loopBackTo is clamped to product-spec / architect / implementer — never forward past qa-acceptance.'

findings.issue: YAML frontmatter description says 'verification -> review -> CI -> release -> monitor' but 'release' and 'monitor' are deleted agents. Also omits security-reviewer and qa-acceptance from the pipeline description. This description is what platforms use to decide when to invoke the skill.
findings.fix: Update to: 'spec -> architecture -> implementation -> verification -> review -> QA -> integration'

findings.issue: Prose mention of 'design-ux' in guidance text: 'so architect and design-ux do not reverse it'. Not functional, but references a deleted agent role.
findings.fix: Change to 'so the architect does not reverse it' (implementer now owns UI work).

findings.issue: QA-acceptance receives the verifier handoff as prior context (line: stagePrompt('qa-acceptance', args, verify)) instead of the reviewer/security-reviewer results. Per the flow diagram (stages.md: R -> QA, SR -> QA), QA follows the quality gates and should receive their context. Non-critical review findings are invisible to QA.
findings.fix: Pass a combined review context to QA. For example: stagePrompt('qa-acceptance', args, { ...verify, findings: [...(review.findings||[]), ...(secReview.findings||[])] })

findings.issue: REQUIRED_SEQUENCE and PRIMARY_PIPELINE include 'release' and 'monitor' after 'integrator'. In the yarn loop path, after integrator succeeds, nextInSequence('integrator') returns 'release', which has no agent file. Stage type union (line 78-93) also includes 6 deleted agents. Not introduced by this PR but was not cleaned up when agents were deleted.
findings.fix: Remove 'release' and 'monitor' from REQUIRED_SEQUENCE and PRIMARY_PIPELINE. Remove deleted agents from the Stage union. Update OPTIONAL_AFTER and LOOP_BACK_TARGETS in team.ts accordingly.

learnings.insight: Grep patterns for deleted-agent cleanup matched path-style references (agents/design-ux) but missed role-name references in prose (nextStage: design-ux). TypeScript files were excluded from file-type globs entirely.
learnings.action: When deleting an agent, grep for the agent name as a bare word across ALL file types (*.ts, *.md, *.json, *.toml, *.js, *.mjs), not just path-style references or a subset of extensions.

learnings.insight: The orchestrator TypeScript runtime (types.ts, team.ts, stages.ts) still models a 10+ agent pipeline including deleted agents. The documentation and agent definitions now describe an 8-agent pipeline. These are out of sync.
learnings.action: After the doc-layer cleanup is merged, schedule a follow-up to align the orchestrator TypeScript runtime types and routing logic with the 8-agent pipeline.
